o1.biggest_strength: Provides explicit management rules for the owner to use (break-even, roll-back thresholds) and shows exact, transparent math for click and trial projections.
o1.biggest_mistake: Instructing the writer to replace the title and meta for the GA4 page on Monday, several days before the new content is actually drafted and ready to publish.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Standardizing the conversion metric across the board (like trials per 1,000 clicks) so the team can easily compare the value of different page groups at a glance.

o2.biggest_strength: Translating the raw data into 'Trials per 1,000 clicks' is a perfect, easily communicable metric. Plus, creating a dedicated page to solve Maya's fear of losing data is a brilliant product-led SEO insight.
o2.biggest_mistake: Relying on the 'strategist' to do a zero-click audit in Month 3, which slightly bends the rule of 'no freelancers' if you were only contracted to deliver this 90-day plan.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: It's virtually a 10 as it stands, though adding a strict protocol on when to roll back a page rewrite if rankings tank would make it entirely bulletproof.

reason: Both plans are exceptional, pragmatic, and directly usable, but Output 2's simplified 'Trials per 1,000 clicks' metric and its targeted content to overcome specific persona objections gives it a slight edge.
